findings.description: The `initial` attribute is replaced by `multiplier` with no backward-compatible alias. Code that reads or assigns `wait.initial` after construction now fails or has no effect.
findings.rationale: Trigger: existing code reads `w.initial` or sets `w.initial = x` on a wait_exponential_jitter instance. Mechanism: `__init__` only sets `self.multiplier`, so reading raises AttributeError, and assigning creates an unused attribute because `__call__` uses `self.multiplier`. Impact: a crash on read, or the wait time silently ignores the assignment.
